title: Stabilized generic rank after deleting finitely many coefficient p-basis elements
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] of characteristic $p>0$ and finite dimension $d\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Fix a subfield $\kappa\subseteq A$ mapping isomorphically onto $A/\mathfrak m$, and a $p$-basis $(\beta_i)_{i\in E}$ of $\kappa$: the finitely supported monomials in the $\beta_i$ with exponents less than $p$ form a basis over $\kappa^p=\{x^p:x\in\kappa\}$. For a finite subset $J\subseteq E$, let $F_J=\kappa^p(\beta_i\mid i\notin J)$, the subfield of $\kappa$ generated by the displayed elements. Set $L=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $M_J=\varprojlim_n\Omega_{A/F_J}/\mathfrak m^n\Omega_{A/F_J}$, where $\Omega$ denotes Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. There is a finite $J_0\subseteq E$ such that for every finite $J\supseteq J_0$ one has $\dim_L(M_J\otimes_A L)=d+|J|$.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.5–2.1.6, printed pp.50–51, especially equations (2.a) and (2.b), for one integral component; the finite exceptional set is supplied there by Proposition 1.2.4.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters], choose $t_1,\ldots,t_d\in\mathfrak m$ with $\sqrt{(t_1,\ldots,t_d)A}=\mathfrak m$. Apply case (a) of [lem-per-parameter-ideal-formal-normalization] with $B=A$, $e=d$ and the given coefficient field $\kappa$. A domain is reduced and its sole minimal prime is $(0)$, so its equidimensional hypothesis is exactly $\dim A=d$. This gives an injective continuous evaluation $R=\kappa[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]\hookrightarrow A$, with $A$ finite over $R$ and $L/K$ finite for $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. The coefficient field is the prescribed one throughout.

source.place: 2.1.4–2.1.6: the fixed parameters and the finite injective parameter map

proof.text: For finite $J\subseteq E$, put $R_J=F_J[[t_1^p,\ldots,t_d^p]]$ and $K_J=\operatorname{Frac}(R_J)\subseteq K$. The statement of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-ring-subfields], specialized to $n=d,m=0$, gives $R$ finite over $R_J$, $K^p\subseteq K_J$, $\bigcap_JK_J=K^p$, and $K_{J\cup J\prime}\subseteq K_J\cap K_{J\prime}$. Each $K/K_J$ is finite: localize finitely many $R_J$-module generators of $R$ at $R_J\setminus\{0\}$. This localization is a domain finite dimensional over $K_J$, hence a field (multiplication by a nonzero element is injective and thus surjective), and equals $K$. The index family is nonempty because $J=\varnothing$ is allowed.

source.place: 2.1.5–2.1.6: the family of cofinite fraction subfields; Stacks Tag 07P5, lemma-power-series-ring-subfields

proof.text: Here is the rank calculation for $K/K_J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-complement-monomial-basis], the bounded monomials $\beta^a$ on $J$ form an $F_J$-basis of $\kappa$. Expanding each coefficient of a series in this finite basis and grouping each exponent vector modulo $p$ gives a unique expansion $f=\sum_{a,b}\beta^at^b f_{a,b}$ with $f_{a,b}\in R_J$ and $0\leq a_i,b_h<p$. Uniqueness follows coefficientwise from that basis. These monomials remain a $K_J$-basis of $K$: any relation has a common nonzero denominator in $R_J$, and for $f/g\in K$ one has $f/g=fg^{p-1}/g^p$ with $g^p\in R_J$. Since $K^p\subseteq K_J$, the family consisting of the $\beta_i$ for $i\in J$ and the $t_h$ for $1\leq h\leq d$ is therefore a relative $p$-basis of $K/K_J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-differentials-basis], its differentials form a $K$-basis of $\Omega_{K/K_J}$. Consequently $\dim_K\Omega_{K/K_J}=d+|J|$.

source.place: 2.1.6: the right hand side of (2.a); explicit bounded-monomial calculation of d+|J|

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-cofinite-subfields-finite-extension-differential-rank] to $L/K$ and the family $(K_J)$. Step 1 supplies finite $L/K$; Step 2 verifies every subfield-family hypothesis. It yields a finite $J_0$ such that the two differential dimensions agree over every cofinite subfield of $K_{J_0}$. For every finite $J\supseteq J_0$, one has $K_J\subseteq K_{J_0}$ by the defining coefficient-subfield inclusion, and Step 2 gives $[K:K_J]<\infty$. Thus $\dim_L\Omega_{L/K_J}=\dim_K\Omega_{K/K_J}=d+|J|$.

Fix such a $J$ and put $B_J=F_J[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]\subseteq R$. The finite coefficient basis of [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-complement-monomial-basis] expands series coefficientwise, so $R$ is a finite free $B_J$-module on the same coefficient monomials. Combining these with the finite $R$-generators of $A$ from Step 1 makes $A$ finite over $B_J$. The evaluation $B_J\to A$ is local and continuous: the variables map into $\mathfrak m$, and its constant field is a subfield of the coefficient field. Apply [lem-per-pth-power-series-completed-differential-comparison] with $F=F_J$, $C=A$ and these $d$ parameters. Its $B_1$ is exactly $R_J$, so the canonical map gives $M_J\cong\Omega_{A/R_J}$.

source.place: 2.1.6: completed/ordinary differential comparison before equation (2.b); EGA 0_IV 21.9.4

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], tensoring the identification in Step 5 with $L$ gives $M_J\otimes_A L\cong\Omega_{L/R_J}$. An $R_J$-derivation on $L$ kills $K_J$: for $0\neq s\in R_J$ the identity $D(s^{-1})=-s^{-2}D(s)=0$ forces it to kill all fractions of $R_J$. Conversely, a $K_J$-derivation kills $R_J$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] therefore identifies $\Omega_{L/R_J}\cong\Omega_{L/K_J}$ with $da\mapsto da$. Taking dimensions and using Step 4 yields $\dim_L(M_J\otimes_A L)=d+|J|$ for every finite $J\supseteq J_0$, as required.

source.place: 2.1.6: the generic fibre identification and equation (2.b)

proof_origin.place: Expose IV 2.1.5–2.1.6 and Proposition 1.2.4; the reversed subscript in the sentence before (2.b) is corrected; completed comparison is EGA 0_IV 21.9.4.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-62304e9fc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no changes. I read ILO IV printed pp.47-51 (1.1.2-1.2.5 including Prop 1.2.4 and its proof, and 2.1.3-2.1.8 including (2.a) and (2.b)) and EGA 0_IV 21.9.4 with its proof. The item statement is unchanged and matches ILO 2.1.6 (2.b) for one integral component. Removing the p-basis existence theorem from stmt_deps is correct because the p-basis is supplied. Small cases: A=F_p(s)[[t]] gives rank 1 at J=empty and 2 at J={s}. A=κ[[x,y]]/(y^p-s x^p) gives rank 2 at J=empty, so J0 is genuinely needed, and rank 2=d+|J| at J={s}. Steps: Step 1 applies case (a) of the normalization node with the prescribed κ; a domain is reduced and equidimensional. Step 2 uses 07P5 with k_J=F_J and A_J=R_J; finiteness of K/K_J is argued in place and is correct. Step 3 expands by coefficient monomials, uses g^p in R_J, gets a relative p-basis because K^p is in K_J, and applies 07P2 to get dimension d+|J|. Step 4 checks every hypothesis of the stabilization node, and J containing J0 gives K_J inside K_J0. Step 5 uses that R is finite free over F_J[[t]], so A is finite over it, and B_1=R_J. Step 6 uses 00RT localization and the D(1/s) argument. Both new nodes are true. The stabilization node is ILO 1.2.4 word for word; I checked it for L=K, separable L/K and L=K(b^{1/p}). For the comparison node I gave my own proof: elements of B_1 have differentials in every m^n Omega, and Omega_{C/B_1} is finite and complete. Neither node is a clause of the item or a duplicate. lem-per-finite-formal-map-differential-cokernel needs a coefficient field and computes differentials relative to the full R. Advisory only: the comparison node could be derived in a few lines from lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal. I found no cycle, no SGA source, and every step is under 900 characters. I accept the five sec-proper-base-change tool_uses. The report's source-error section about the reversed subscript in ILO 2.1.6 is accurate.
